title: Adaptive Log Gateway for Structured Events and Trace Joins
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current log ingestion path handles many formats (plain text stdout, ad-hoc JSON, syslog, and agent-side enrichments). This results in inconsistent fields, missing correlation IDs, and high variance in downstream query latency. Several services emit duplicate fields (trace_id vs traceId vs x-trace), and some high-volume producers flood the pipeline with verbose debug events, driving up Loki storage and query cost.

Goal: Implement an adaptive log gateway service that normalizes incoming events into a canonical structured schema, performs deterministic trace/link extraction and join hints, supports dynamic sampling for noisy sources, and routes enriched events to Loki (logs) and our metrics/derivation pipeline (for event-derived metrics). The gateway must: preserve tenant isolation, support per-service config, and introduce minimal end-to-end latency.

Scope: Ingest gateway + enrichment plugins (trace mapping, tenant mapping, redaction), per-service YAML config store, dynamic sampling control API, and router logic to fan-out to Loki and metric pipeline. Not in scope: full replacement of existing fleet agents; this will coexist and be phased in per-service.
acceptance_criteria:
- Gateway deployed behind API layer and accepting events from Vector/Fluentd/stderr-forwarders.
- 90% of test traffic (mixture of JSON/plain) is transformed into canonical schema with fields: timestamp, service, env, level, message, trace_id, span_id (if present), tenant_id, event_type, attributes.
- Trace extraction heuristics map >95% of requests with a parent trace_id when trace headers exist, and canonicalize common header variants (trace_id, traceId, X-B3-TraceId, Traceparent).
- Dynamic sampling policy can be updated via API and affects ingestion rates within 60s for target producers.
- No more than 5ms median added latency and <10ms p95 for the logging path in the dataplane under normal load.
- Unit and integration tests covering schema normalization, redaction, and routing.
- Dashboards created: Ingest Rate, Dropped Events, Normalization Failures, Trace Link Coverage, Per-service Sample Rate.
- Rollback plan tested in staging: revert routing to previous collector with zero data loss for 30 minutes of test traffic.
tech_notes:
Design: lightweight Go microservice placed in the ingest tier. Key components:
- Parser chain: format detection -> schema normalizer (field mapping rules + JSON schema validation) -> enrichment hooks (trace mapper, tenant resolver, IP-geo, sampling decision) -> redaction/pii scrubber -> router.
- Schema registry: simple git-backed YAML mapping per service that maps incoming variants to canonical fields. We will provide a small builtin rule set for common libs (node, python, java).
- Trace mapping: heuristics for header precedence + fallback to parse message for embedded trace/context. Use deterministic key 'trace_id' (lowerhex 32 chars) and support Traceparent/W3C & B3.
- Sampling: token-bucket-based adaptive sampler per service+env with server-side override via control API; decisions emitted as metric and annotation on events.
- Backpressure: when Loki/metrics pipeline is congested gateway applies sampling and local persistent buffer (1GB cap) with LRU eviction policy.
- Security: redact fields matching configured regexes before storing in transient buffers. All configs fetched from internal config service with RBAC and audit.

Trade-offs:
- Doing normalization in gateway increases CPU but reduces storage and query cost downstream.
- Keeping config git-backed makes rollouts predictable but slower; dynamic API allows quick fixes.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1: MVP parser chain, simple schema rules, W3C+B3 trace extraction, basic router to staging Loki.
- Phase 2: per-service configs, sampling API, redaction rules, metrics emission, production rollout for low-volume services.
- Phase 3: auto-suggest mapping rules (heuristic learner) and UI in Console for per-service tuning.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy gateway to staging, route e2e test traffic from synthetic generators.
2) Onboard 3 low-risk services (platform-auth, metrics-proxy, webhook-ingress) for a 48h soak. Monitor 'Normalization Failures' and 'Trace Link Coverage'.
3) Gradually onboard mid-volume services, adjusting default sample rates to keep Loki ingest below budget threshold.
4) Enable gateway for high-volume producers behind a sampled roll-forward (start at 1% sample, increase while observing cost metrics).
5) Switch production routing for remaining services as mapping rules stabilize.
6) Full cutover guarded by automatic rollback triggers: >2x expected ingest, >1% normalization failure for 1h, or any regression in trace link coverage by >10%.

Rollback: revert routing in service mesh to previous collector, or disable gateway feature flag per-tenant. We will test the rollback in staging before production rollout.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for parser chain and normalization rules.
- Integration tests: run against staging Loki and metrics pipeline, assert events arrive with canonical fields.
- Load tests: 10k events/s synthetic, observe added latency and memory usage.
- Chaos tests: simulate downstream Loki slowness and verify gateway applies sample/backpressure correctly.
- Privacy tests: feed test events containing PII patterns and verify redaction rules remove them before buffer or routing.
- E2E verification: automate trace-join tests that assert a transaction spanning API->runtime->worker has consistent trace_id across logs and appears in Trace Link Coverage dashboard.
notes:
Recent spike in Loki costs traced to unbounded debug logging from billing-relay; this gateway should allow per-service emergency sampling as part of the incident response playbook.

Design review feedback (2026-03-05): Security requested mandatory redaction rules for credit-card-like patterns and an audit log of any config changes. Product suggested a Console UI hook for adjusting sample rates per-tenant.

Open questions:
- Do we enforce canonical trace_id length/format at ingestion or accept legacy variants downstream? (Current plan: normalize to lower-hex 32 char when possible, otherwise attach original header in attributes.)
- Persistence strategy for local buffer (file vs embedded RocksDB) — preferring file-backed append log for simplicity.

Next steps: finalize sampling API design, implement initial redaction plugin, and schedule cross-team onboarding sessions with platform and billing teams.
